author: vladimir_ea
content: I have a couple of questions on this proposal: https://www.potuz.net/posts/gloas-circuit-breaker/

author: vladimir_ea
content:
- what is meant by missing payload? I am assuming that it means either not delivered but also includes delivered but invalid? 

the comment that most missing blocks are caused by large builder bugs suggests that this is the case, b/c currently missed slots can occur when the winning block is invalid (e.g. incorrect state root)

author: vladimir_ea
content: but i do not belive missed slots often occur becuase a large builder has failed to deliver the layload.

author: vladimir_ea
content:
"so that on a single failure we blacklist the builder for just one epoch, but on two consecutive failures during 5 epochs the builder is permanently banned until a restart"

if a 'single failure' includes invalid payloads (not just undelivered payload - which it must do to protect against DoS?) then this seems overly aggressive?

why is it assumed that a single invalid is a systemic error requiring a curcuit break? surely 2 consecutive invlaid blocks from the same builder would be more rationale circuit break? what do <@&1458826346896687229> think?

author: vladimir_ea
content: also I find the phrase "two consecutive failures during 5 epochs" somewhat confusing - what does it mean exactly?

author: ajsutton
content: There's really no excuse for building any bad block.

author: vladimir_ea
content: right, because all software is always perfect, no excuses.

author: vladimir_ea
content: back in the real world though, it does happen that invalid blocks win slots - this happens currently, albeit rarely, becuase none of the existing builders are actually perfect.  But these problems are in almost all cases transitory issues confined to a single slot.

author: vladimir_ea
content: so the question is whether it makes sense to ban a builder for an epoch following a single slot error?
